## Details

### elekloader

Mod loader: user supplies the stock OS file, the tool builds the custom .syx locally. Device table in the README (3016dca, 2026-11-08): Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1/Keys supported; Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.12 experimental; Octatrack 1.40C supported (linkable core boots on an MKII); Model:Cycles and Model:Samples 1.13 supported (builds work on both units); Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 supported; Analog Four MKII 1.56 experimental proof of concept (hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit). Canonical repo is unclear: the forum post also embeds github.com/elekloader/elekloader (web app at elekloader.github.io/elekloader); forks exist (AvroraPolnareff, naturarum, toonst, simonjohansson); none is listed, as none has changes of its own. Forum: builder issue reported 2026-10-19. Licence GPL-2.0-or-later. 2026-11-10 (8daa2ea): the shop's list, forms and bots moved to elekloader/shop (#338); mods are submitted there. machine-pages 1.8-1.10, machines-dn1 0.5/0.6 and machines-dn2 0.5 add mono machines and MIDI CCs (emulator-tested per TESTS.md). The linker now refuses odd jump targets into mod RAM after a Digitakt II froze at boot (I61). The README offers a Windows .exe; not every release carries the macOS .dmg. 2026-11-10 (main): core-ar2 0.13 opens the Rytm MKII's TEST slots 44-52 to mod machines, adds per-voice trig and velocity getters, screen calls through stock's routines and per-mod knob ids; machine-pages 1.7 tagged. 2026-11-12 (main): core-a4mk2 0.6 brings core-ar2 0.10-0.13's foundations to the Analog Four MKII (field defaults, the modified mark, the project-save event, payloads, knob looks, screen calls) and a 37.7 MB mods' area. Builds pick older core or helper versions by themselves when a mod patches a place a newer one took (Tone+FX's Digitakt files and Digi EQ 1.0c link with DT1 core 4.0 only; OB-1 0.6 with machine-pages 1.2), and released versions stay available while a listed mod needs them. 2026-11-13 (main): a third file family, ELE2, for the Analog Rytm MKI OS 1.74 (Modwerk's Rytm MKI research holds the measurements behind the profile); the README's table also names 1.73, the profile only 1.74. core-ot 0.9-0.40 opens about 40 more Octatrack events and tables to mods (mutes, sequencer moments, LFO waves, popup rows, PATTERN SETTINGS and PERSONALIZE rows, the playback increment, card file calls, the engine task's jobs, a block to DSP core 1). 2026-11-15 (FORMAT, SDK, CORES): std1 'standard events': a mod that sets events std1 subscribes to device- neutral event names, each core maps them to its own tables, and a subscription the core does not map is refused at link time; std1 and native mods link in one build. core-a4mk2 0.7 is the first core with it and adds native A4 events for knob turns, the analog voice frame and modulation edits. A frame-check build that copied one voice's analog frame words over another's silenced track 1 and was fixed in 0.3 (unit or emulator not stated). 2026-11-16 (docs/CORES.md, DRIVE.md, FORMAT.md, core-dn1 README): on the Digitone mk1 the build descriptor now carries the stock bytes of each flashed range (ABI 1.2), and TELOS's linker refuses a +Drive mod site that is not stock on the unit, overlaps the flashed build or another mod, or a region outside a free area (link codes 21-28). core-dn1 5.4's core_stock_info copies the OS image to 0x44200000 before the OS runs. 2026-11-17 (ADAPTING, FORMAT, core-ot, settings-ot, dspload-ot, core-a4mk2 READMEs): core-ot 0.41/0.42 add 16 Octatrack events (tempo, scenes, card mount and USB DISK MODE, previews, recorder commands, pages, track select, windows, crossfader, pattern select and edits, arrangement); new dspload-ot 0.2 sends DSP code at run time (mod.json `dsp_load`), also for TELOS card mods; refusal code 23 `early` for a site the OS ran before the +Drive or card link. On the Analog Four MKII the lock service is now checked on a unit. 2026-11-18 (v0.11.0, docs/DRIVE.md, CORES.md, drive-loader-a4mk2 and drive-loader-ar2 READMEs): v0.11.0 ships the newest core of every device, core-a4mk2 0.9 included. The Analog Four MKII gets its own +Drive mods loader (drive-loader-a4mk2 0.1, not yet run): stock 1.56 keeps the +Drive as raw sectors with no file system, so the loader keeps its own two-copy store in sectors stock never addresses. The Rytm loader (0.6) now reads each file into the +Drive area itself (a 64 KB floor replaces the 512 KB staging buffer), and +Drive mods may hold storage fields, sites over the OS, claims, tables of their own, knob ids and std1 subscriptions where the build's descriptor flags allow (descriptor ABI 1.3). drive-loader-ar2's README asks for core-ar2 0.14 while core-ar2's mod.json at the tag reads 0.13. New A4 MKII check mods for live recording, the sequencer and moments (read as expected in the emulator, 2026-11-14).

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument.org and the repo (read 2026-10-31): canonical repo is github.com/elekloader/elekloader (183 commits, 103 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later); web app moved to elekloader.github.io/elekloader; the Mac app was absent from v0.9.0 because signing secrets need renewing. v0.9.0 cores: core-4.1 and core-4.1-os1.54 (Digitakt mk1), core-dn1-4.1.1 and -os1.44 (Digitone mk1), core-ar2-0.8 (Analog Rytm MKII 1.74), core-ot-0.8 (Octatrack 1.40C), core-mc-0.3 (Model:Cycles), core-ms-0.1 (Model:Samples), core-a4 0.1-0.4 (Analog Four MKII 1.56). Kit 0.7.0 catalog: 19 cores, 88 mods. machine-pages 1.2/1.3/1.5 need core 3.0+ on Digitakt mk1 and refuse NEIGHBOR 0.6, SOPHIE 1.1.13 and digichain-based machine mods beside them; fxkit 0.1 gives Digitone effect mods a shared mixer, two LFOs, pattern p-locks and a CPU guard; core-dn1 4.1 adds ev_note_queue; kit 0.6.0 gives 4.0 cores larger RAM areas (256 KB Digitakt, 1.25 MB Digitone). docs/ includes AGENTS.md, DEVICES.md, MACHINES-DN2, SHARC-DN2, CORES, FORMAT, BUILDING, ADAPTING (not all read yet - see hardware/MINING.md). The earlier irpina/elekloader repo is where the author's older releases lived._

_Related: uses tool `digikit` (README: checks or gates run in digikit's emulator (not shipped)) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### elektron-firmware-tool

C, MIT licence. Unpacks Elektron .syx firmware and repacks it as a valid file. Lists Analog Heat MKI, MKII and +FX among supported devices - currently the only Analog Heat-relevant tool we found. Forum listing: 113 stars, repo created 2026-07-22, "last commit 1 month ago" at the time of listing.

_Sources: forum mod list (mods.php?id=7), forum thread 8_

### Overtone

Python 3.11+ patcher (patcher/patch.py) that builds Overtone from the user's own OS 1.12 and only saves the result if it matches the tested build byte for byte; install via Elektron Transfer over USB. Adds machines SOPHIE, MACHINEDRUM, LOOP, THRU, per-track insert effects, envelope followers, two arpeggiators, parameter slides and GROOVE (replaces swing). 1.0.1 fixes installing an OS sent with Transfer while Overtone runs. About 160 checks per build in two emulators (digikit for the main OS, a SHARC emulator for the DSP program); author states 1.0.1 passes all of them, is played on a Digitone II and Transfer installs were checked on the unit. Opening Overtone projects on stock OS is untested. Recovery section is detailed (FUNC + TRIG 4, DIN MIDI, ~15 min). AGPL-3.0-or-later (includes dnfw), 5 commits. Related: dnfw, digikit, dn2-cfw, Schwung Sophie (MIT), and the author's digitone-2-modding-skill used with Claude Code. 2026-11-17 (README, v1.6): arps, LFOs and followers also work on MIDI tracks to play and modulate external gear; a follower can listen to the main mix or the audio inputs; a trig with only locks now slides too.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument: v1.1 (2026-10-30) reworks GROOVE with presets, a random drift control, random weights and arrow-key editing, and restores FUNC + TEMPO as tap tempo; v1.0.1 (2026-10-29) fixes installing Elektron's OS or an Overtone update with Transfer while Overtone runs._

### SYXGRID v2

Free browser-based pattern/sequence editor, not a firmware mod. Repo includes sysexmap/, a public reverse-engineered SysEx format map (CC BY 4.0): 45 mappings, map version 1.13.0, each with a confidence level (A = hardware-confirmed on a DN2: 23; B = corpus-confirmed by repo fixtures: 12; C = inherited, one value exercised: 9; D = unknown, do not rely: 1). Narrowed by bisection on 2026-09-08 against a Digitone II (OS 1.10E) and a Digitakt II. Not decoded: parameter locks, sound parameters (filter, amp, FX, LFO), synth machine choice. Needs the DN2 in SYSEX RECEIVE mode; Web MIDI needs Chromium over HTTPS or localhost (Chrome/Edge 152 break SysEx receive on macOS). App is AGPLv3 since v22.46 (MIT through v22.37). 6 commits.

### DN2 DT2 firmware research

Source-only recipes for Digitone II firmware with six Digitakt II sample machines (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE), stereo samples, sample browsing, DT2 parameter graphics and SLICES trig mode. Recorder adds recording/resampling, source selection, normalization, trimming, audition, saving to +Drive and optional track assignment; VOICE cycles Voice Setup, Sample Manager and Recorder. Class-compliant USB audio provides 42 capture channels at 48 kHz/24 bit (MAIN, tracks 1-16, DELAY, REVERB, CHORUS, INPUT as stereo pairs) and a stereo return. R012 needs only the official DN2 1.11 and DT2 1.16 OS files; silent compatibility data replaces the private sample bank, and users load their own playable samples afterward. Native and browser builders verify exact inputs and the output: 2,563,872 bytes, SHA-256 4a2742a4...63a3a9a. The browser builds locally without uploading files; neither builder flashes the instrument. No firmware images or samples are distributed. Historical exact T1E2/R003/R008/R011 builds still require their original private sample bank. R011 fixed USB publication stalling after project changes by selecting its candidate destination from current DMA START while preserving ownership checks; R012 retains that fix. Owner-confirmed stock audio, samples, Recorder and USB audio on R012, including after project changes. Stable does not mean exhaustive validation: exact trimmed-file comparison, full Recorder-source coverage, endurance and end-to-end USB latency remain unverified. Builds on dnfw (angellinares/dn2_firmware_explore), selache, digikit and elektron-firmware-tool. AGPL-3.0-or-later. 2026-11-03: README warns new users NOT to install R012 yet. R012 mounts an existing sample filesystem but does not create one on a DN2 that never had it; symptoms are 0% Free / 0 bytes in Transfer, stalled uploads, Connection failed. The author says stock FORMAT +DRIVE, EMPTY RESET and FACTORY RESET do not create it and can erase projects; at that point an on-device formatter was still in development. R013 subsequently added FORMAT SAMPLES with erase confirmation; formatting, restart, capacity and post-format uploads were checked on the owner's unit. Owner testing of R012 had used storage prepared during development. An earlier track-2 saved-project reload report was an unsaved checkpoint; R022 addresses a separate, reproduced failure to refresh the sample table in the unsaved working-state backup. This does not establish recovery from an interrupted write or USB freeze.

### digikit

Native Rust emulator that runs the ColdFire and SHARC+ firmware together, with front panel, display and audio, plus a web panel (WASM core), a Tauri desktop app, the patch toolchain "patchkit" (applies modules to the user's own .syx), a headless scenario runner with pinned PCM hashes, a control socket for patch injection and DSP/ColdFire analysis databases with Ghidra tooling. README caveats: the DSP "does not run in real time yet", the browser host is parked on branch wip/browser-host, "no patched firmware has been installed on a device", and recovery via the bootstrap menu is "not tested on hardware". patchkit refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8. 2026-11-12 (b657f37, via altstrument): a USB take-over for fast sample transfer in the workbench with a read-back hash check per file, a diagnostic module that reads card information, a restructured SDK, fixes to the card image and the patch kit on Windows. 982 commits, AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra section-7 terms (attribution, origin, names) in NOTICE; page shows 46 open issues. GitHub marks it as not a fork. The org ElekLabs has 2 public repos: digikit and a fork of js216/selache. Original author: the GitHub profile m-dwyer is named "Em D" (Melbourne), which is exactly the credit ElekLabs' NOTICE requires ("digikit by Em D"); Overtone credits digikit to "Em D" as well. The earlier repo m-dwyer/digikit (196 commits, 4 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later, README at the time: "no audio", last visible file HANDOVER-2026-09-16) shows no move/archive notice and does not mention ElekLabs. ElekLabs has no public members, so the pages themselves do not show who runs it; the maintainer (user of this repo) states that Em D develops in ElekLabs/digikit (2026-10-31, not verifiable on the pages). The licence changed from GPL-2.0-or-later to AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra terms. Treat both repos as one project line, ElekLabs/digikit being the current one. Mod READMEs that say "digikit's emulator" mean this project. 2026-11-14 (finding 123 rewritten, findings 128-129, docs/MODULES.md, docs/ADDRMAP.md): the USB take-over is deleted (its commands answer E_STATE); core/usb-bulk-audio adds a vendor bulk OUT interface to the USB AUDIO/MIDI configuration at boot, so there is no mode switch (a probe sent 200 MB at 28 MB/s while audio played; real uploads 3.38 MB/s on a DN2, 2.74 MB/s on a DT2). Runtime 0.7.0: modules declare machines and effects with builder calls and the runtime commits them at once or refuses; a module of another major.minor is refused (E_CONTRACT); the patched-in content macros are gone. An address map names code addresses in crash records and profiles; the debug module can keep a card log that survives a crash. Finding 128 (static): the SHARC hook sites cannot move into run-time services, because the ColdFire uploads the whole DSP image before the card is readable. 2026-11-15 (MODULE-AUTHORING, design/module-sdk, handover): modules no longer declare their DSP cycles; module:check measures the worst steady block and stores a per-voice or per-effect DSP cost in the package, and one shared rule (largest voice cost x voices + effect costs within the headroom) now runs in the boot planner, the menu, patchkit fit and the web Transfer tab, which refuses a selection over the limit ('DSP LOAD need > free'). Modules built for the old descriptor must be rebuilt. Runtime limits now listed: 512 KiB arena, 64 KiB per module, 8 machine rows, 3 FX slots, DSP area 512 KiB (DT2) / 320 KiB (DN2). The SDK sample kernel has since landed (2026-11-16): the Shot machine fell from about 5,000 to about 2,450 (DT2) / 2,660 (DN2) emulator instructions a block, bit-identical. 2026-11-16 (findings 130 and 132, sdk/dsp/REGISTERS.md, handovers; runtime 0.8.2, untagged): one generated DSP register contract for module code (clobber, keep, stack, never_write), checked by patchkit build but only as a warning so far; the fx, machines, samples and lfo services are separate crates, the step before loadable services; module DSP tests moved to a SHARC-only rig (about 45 s instead of about 21 min). Finding 103 was partly withdrawn: several values reported as measured on silicon came from probe instructions the old assembler had mis-encoded (see digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md). No new unit run in this period. 2026-11-17 (findings 133-135, plans usb-fast-batch, runtime-slimming, r12-8-sharc-stubs, digikit-hot-reload, handovers; runtime 0.8.3, untagged): a Fast USB speed round ran on a DN2 (OS 1.12) and a DT2 (OS 1.17) on 2026-11-16 with every file hash-checked: one store-table commit for up to 16 files, copy/write overlap and fewer +Drive steps per file took a sample pack from 2.42 to 3.56 MB/s (DN2) and 2.32 to 3.07 MB/s (DT2) and a 9.8 MB file to 4.37 / 4.13 MB/s; a cached USB receive was slower and was dropped. Finding 133 (static): the card takes one transfer at a time under global mutexes, so parallel writers cannot help. Services become separate .dks files bound to the user's own firmware at install (patchkit bind; bound files hold firmware bytes and are never committed): lfo.dks is merged, Transfer installs the services a module needs (both emulator-tested), fx.dks and machines.dks are on a branch. Hot reload is an active plan again (finding 135, static firmware facts), not built. Facts in devices/digitakt-2.md. 2026-11-18 (findings 136-141, devices/syntakt.toml, plan syntakt.md): Syntakt OS 1.42 support in the emulator only. The emulator runs MAIN and the second ColdFire (section 7) in lock step, with digital audio (analog tracks silent); patchkit builds a no-seal 1.42 image that changes only section 3 and refuses sections 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 and 8; the runtime, menu, health and input adapters boot on the emulated 1.42 and load the debug module over emulated USB MIDI. Nothing has been flashed to a Syntakt. The DT2 and DN2 device files gained [protect] windows (hardware blocks a content module may not address; the packer refuses such a module) and [container] roles; the bulk OUT interface (core/usb-bulk-audio) is now in the default device image of both. 2026-11-18 (docs/PATCHING, MODULES, ARCHITECTURE, plans runtime-and-services and r12-8-sharc-stubs, port files): machines and effects are run-time modules only; patchkit now refuses a patch-time machine or effect row. The services machines.dks and fx.dks have landed: unbound files hold no firmware bytes, `patchkit bind` makes the stock tails from the user's own firmware, and Transfer installs the services a module needs (emulator example on DN2 1.12: machines.dks 29,718 bytes). The SHARC hook sites now jump through 16 slot words that a service fills (4 used). core/usb-bulk-audio (Fast USB beside USB audio) moved from a separate patch set into the default `device` and `device-introblank` sets on both devices. `patchkit pack` refuses a content module whose code or data holds an address inside a device's protected windows (flash controller, FPGA, peer buses). The DN2 OS 1.11 port file grew from 277 to 358 anchors (1.12: 359), adding the USB, card-driver, DSP voice and link anchors. No new unit run in these files.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument (2026-10-31): main @ 283bb90, untagged, described as patch toolchain AND run-time module system plus emulator; AGPL-3.0-or-later. Its device-side tools (dkupload, dklog) belong to that module system. 2026-11-08 (PR #321, finding 117): loadable boot screens. ### dn2_firmware_explore

Tools to inspect, modify and rebuild Digitone firmware (dnfw, CLI and browser), plus 17 mods for Digitone II 1.11 (Waverider wavetable machine, LFO4, arp modes, LFO waves, FX destinations and others), each with a version and a changelog. The ~80% recovery-path stall once listed as open was the MIDI link, not the image (settled 2026-09-11). AGPL-3.0-or-later. The container tools also unpack and rebuild Digitone / Digitone Keys (MKI) OS files (tests use DN1 OS 1.42A; its container is unsigned), and its parameter search on DN1 images is "not yet reliable" per the CLI; there are no mods for the MKI (README and source read 2026-11-11). 2026-11-12 (docs/os-versions.md, issue #382): port to OS 1.12 under way: address maps by instruction anchors decided all 778 mod sites (594 same bytes, 184 relocated), the platform has a 1.12 spec and a 1.12 test image boots in the emulator; every mod is to get a 1.12 build beside its 1.11 build, 1.11 stays the default until all are ported. 2026-11-13 (docs/os-versions.md): stock 1.12 touched no RAM from 0x46700000 up in an emulator run, bootscreen moves to 0x467e8000 on 1.12, the heap arena moves +0x1000 on 1.12 (S22), and lfo4 builds for 1.12 in the emulator. 2026-11-16 (README, docs/sendloop.md, docs/mods-page.md): new mod sendloop rewrites the ColdFire loop that copies each 1,344-word DSP frame into the transfer buffer (4 instead of 7 instructions a word, one 32-bit write instead of two), about 4 points less main-processor load, confirmed on hardware on OS 1.11. Every build now gets a MODS page (SETTINGS > SYSTEM > MODS) that lists the OS, the build name, the tool's commit and each mod's version; its code and rows sit at 0x46798000. 2026-11-18 (README): the sendloop mod is now on by default in builds.

Hardware-confirmed mods: lfo4, arpmodes, lfowaves, midiarp, layermidi, fxmod and the lfolength fix (2026-10-09, audio track). No GitHub releases - tags are work snapshots._

### dn2-cfw

Public lab notebook: notes, tools and new effects, no Elektron firmware included. Seven builds run on real hardware per README (EF01 renamed stock, FLG1 flanger replacing the chorus, FTD1 + one-head tape delay, DH01 core/hook bus with a MIDI test mod, FTN1 renamed screens, GT00 parameter table moved, GT01 + 17 hidden rows for the 3-band compressor); not yet on the unit: the 3-band compressor and a Space-Echo-style delay (fx/spaceecho.c). Rule of the author: "nothing counts as working until it has run on my unit". Getting started (README): macOS on Apple silicon (Linux likely for most), Python 3, the user's own Digitone_II_OS1_12.syx in elektron-firmware/, upstream tools cloned into vendor/ (VENDOR.md) - for digikit and elekloader the author's forks on branch dn2-1.12 (digikit: 1.12 support, audio clock, DIN MIDI, LEDs, live play; elekloader: Digitone II 1.12 profile and the core-dn2 hook bus), commands scripts/dn2-emu-112.sh all, scripts/dn2-live.sh, fx make test/renders, tools/brickcheck/brickcheck CANDIDATE.syx (12 checks, must pass before any flash). README gives no step-by-step flashing procedure. Docs: ROADMAP.md, HANDOFF.md (later entries supersede earlier), FIRMWARE.md (sha256s), VENDOR.md, docs/parameter-table-growth.md, notes/ (one report per task, claims marked [verified] or [inferred]), analysis/ (class hierarchy recovered from RTTI). 28 commits, GPL-2.0(-or-later).

### OpenBridge - Digitone II

A Linux (x86_64) implementation of Overbridge for the Digitone II, as a VST3 plugin (JUCE; the standalone app was dropped on 2026-11-12): 42 channels of USB audio out and 8 in with clock-drift compensation, every sound parameter of the 16 tracks readable and editable with DAW automation, a mixer, and a preset browser for kit presets and the +Drive library. The README first said it was written from an analysis of the Overbridge 2.26.10 installer and measurements on the device, with Elektron's artwork extracted at build time from the user's own installer; since 2026-11-12 it says neither, and the build needs no installer. Delay time shows as a raw value. Not affiliated with Elektron. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-12.

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-12, README (2026-11-12)_

### DN2 mk2 Mod (dn2mk2-firmware)

Adds Digitakt II sample machines (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE) with sample browser and recorder, PERC (34 Machinedrum machines incl. TRX, EFM, GND, P-I), Monomachine voices (SID 6581, DPRO WAVE/DDRW/DENS, VO-6) and a CPU guard. Browser-based patcher builds from the user's own files ("nothing is uploaded") and saves only if the output sha256 matches a build that passed scripts/ship_gate.py. Hardware: README says verification is pending per version; FIRMWARE.md says nearly every v0.21-v0.33 entry was checked in emulators and "not seen on hardware yet". Main open problem: DSP time (heavy voices cut sound). Flashing a 1.12 unit takes it back to a 1.11 base, projects saved under the newer OS may not open. 1,491 commits, 8 stars, AGPL-3.0-or-later. FIRMWARE.md says built firmware is kept on the repo's `builds` branch (not main) - unlike most projects here, which only ship patchers; we link only to the repo and docs, not to builds. Withdrawn builds: v0.4-v0.7 (oversized image). v0.38 (2026-11-02): Direct Jump state kept in its own +Drive sector (0x6FF000); per-project sample lists at +Drive 0x6D0000-0x6E02FF, two checked copies each. Root cause of the silent new samples: the DSP plays a pool slot only below the directory's count, and live adds did not update the count. v0.39 (2026-11-03): recordings had kept only ~2 ms since v0.38 because the DSP recorder took words 2-4 of every new link command as source, channel and threshold, and v0.38 sent a check command at every take's start; now only the recorder's own commands set them. 2026-11-15: the first test build, v0.54-t1 STEREO, is announced as a GitHub pre-release on the owner's request and listed under TEST in the patcher, not as the latest. Testers are asked to check hard-panned stereo files on headphones, filters and overdrive on both sides, and a fifth voice falling back to the mono mix. Next: stereo comb filters and sends, and the stock NAME screen for sample names. 2026-11-16 (FIRMWARE.md, release notes v0.54-v0.56): each build passed its gate in the emulator (54-56 gate steps) and is cleared to flash; unit results for these three builds are not reported yet. A DDRW sound saved with BR above 0 sounds grittier from v0.56. 2026-11-17 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.57, docs/flex-pool.md): v0.57 FLEXMUTE is gated (56 gate steps) and cleared. It answers a tester's unit report on v0.55/v0.56: MUTE SRC muted the source as soon as a take existed, and some tracks could not be unmuted until a power cycle. Now the SRC track drops out only while a FLEX voice has its note on and is heard, and comes back about 0.2 s after the note ends; known issue: a long gap between FLEX notes un-mutes the source. FLEX takes still measure about 6 dB below their source (to be fixed). The v0.54-t1 STEREO test build was taken off the patcher's list because stereo samples do not play yet (altstrument, 2026-11-16). Planned next: microtonal scales in KB SETUP and a one-handed keyboard latch. 2026-11-18 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.58): v0.58 SCALES added two microtonal scales to KB SETUP (PR12, a 12-note just tuning laid out as Chromatic; PM12, its 7-note minor laid out as Aeolian), retuning each voice by cents above ROOT. It passed its 57-step gate but crashed a unit in a chord MODE and was pulled from the patcher on 2026-11-17; the code is reverted on main, a fix is on a branch. Withdrawn builds now: v0.4-v0.7 (oversized image), v0.58 (crash). Planned next: MON on the recorder, the Monomachine FM+ machines, a per-track 4-band EQ, arp scale lock and in-key transpose.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): v0.34 TIMING: P-I voices that stayed dead after v0.33's guard muted them are now reset on the next note; a FUNC-held readout shows V1D (bad data in a voice's delay memory) or V1X (elsewhere); new USB diag tool tools/dn2diag.py reads the guard record and scans DSP memory for bad values; the ColdFire emulator now fires the audio interrupt at its real rate, and DSP tests charge memory like the chip. v0.35 SWEEP (2026-11-01): fixes only (MACHINE SEL filter list, +DRIVE preview retrigger, SYN-held values, LOAD TO PROJ, deleted folders, LFO page names). Open: why P-I / VO-6 voices go bad on the instrument. Same scope as armio's T1E2 (DT2 sample machines on DN2 1.11). v0.36 VOICES: the fixed two-voice cap on Monomachine tracks is gone (the real-time DSP guard decides): SID, VO-6, DENS and DPRO WAVE play 4-note chords, DDRW 2; when there is no room the oldest voice is dropped cleanly; DDRW/DENS tables moved to fast memory; a Diagnostics section in the import page reads the instrument after a silent voice. ROADMAP after v0.40 (2026-11-03): engine-direction talk (a build without Monomachine; the MM chord glitch first), slides on the sample and Machinedrum machines' own continuous controls, Octatrack-style rec trigs, then a comparison with heavylight's Capicola time-stretch. The roadmap also plans to read Aggregat (export DB, research map) before new DN2 work. 2026-11-09: FASCIA (modal percussion) was built and pulled for size, planned for v0.48; FLEX is to replace BOUNCE; Capicola is on hold at its author's request. 2026-11-12: FASCIA moves to a separate second firmware without the Machinedrum and Monomachine machines (entry dn2-rift); docs/stereo-assessment.md plans stereo samples by running the DN2's mono per-track chain twice, on its own branch. 2026-11-14: test builds from feature branches (named X.Y-tN, first planned 0.54-t1 for stereo) are gated like releases and listed under TEST in the patcher, never as the latest; queued after it: a rewrite of the Machinedrum and Monomachine engines in the project's own lighter code on a removable branch, a full optimisation and stability sweep measured against stock, and a study of reusing the stock NAME screen for sample names._

### digitone-2-modding-skill

Agent skill (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor; install with `npx skills add`) for developing Digitone II firmware mods: ColdFire MAIN OS patching in C, SHARC DSP audio code, verification in two emulators (digikit + a whole-DSP SHARC emulator), rebuild/re-sign/flash over USB. Encodes stock-firmware addresses, hook sites, the ColdFire-to-DSP frame format, free memory and "hardware rules the emulators cannot check, which each once silenced a real unit" - read on 2026-10-31 via SKILL.md and references/*.md (SKILL.md has 20 rules incl. whole 32-byte boot blocks, stock encodings only, no L2 above 0x200B0000, never read unwritten DDR, 2 MiB image / section 7 under 1 MiB, stop after two failed flashes; scripts include hwrules.py, shapecheck.py, encodecheck.py, bootblocks.py, sim.py/simc.py, cfmod.py, rpc_flash.py). Facts and rules are folded into hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md and hardware/common/agent-workflow.md. Note: tree pages are blocked for our fetcher by robots.txt; the blob pages were readable. Examples: double_time (sequencer clock hook), track_trim (-6 dB on track 1). Needs Python 3.11+, dnfw, m68k GCC, digikit. MIT (digikit-derived files GPL-2.0), 2 commits, 10 stars. Overtone was built with it. Closest existing relative of this repo's hardware/ folder.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument: main @ 84c8cd3 (2026-10-29), no tagged releases; brick-risk flag set ("flashing carries a known, documented risk of damaging the device")._

_Related: uses tool `digikit` (catalogue notes: verification in digikit); uses tool `dn2-firmware-explore` (README: prerequisite dnfw (container, signing, C builds)) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### coldfire-rs

Rust stack for ColdFire V4e (MCF5441x): toolchain (rustc_codegen_gcc + libgccjit for m68k-elf), runtime, PAC generated from an SVD, and an Embassy HAL (GPIO, PIT, INTC, eDMA, UART, DSPI, eSDHC eMMC block reads, SSI/I2S, USB OTG device mode). Not an emulator and not an Elektron mod: the README never mentions Elektron or digikit, the only link is the topic tag "digitakt". It is relevant here because digikit names the MCF54415 as the control CPU of Digitakt II (and the Digitone II is described as ColdFire too). Drivers were run on the author's own MCF54415 board. README: API is young and may change before 1.0. 33 commits, Apache-2.0 OR MIT. Same owner also has deluge-sdk (Synthstrom Deluge, out of scope). Org shows no public members; no relation to ElekLabs/Em D found.

_Sources: GitHub README, FirestormAudio profile page_

### digi-roll-studio

Native Rust desktop sequencer for Digitakt II, Digitone II and Analog Four, built from digi-roll. Writes to hardware: README recommends throwaway projects. Safe-write ceremony of five rules (re-read and back up the destination pattern first, OS build on an allowlist, user confirmation, change only needed bytes, read back and byte-compare). Gen-2 dump protocol (digis) vs gen-1 (Analog Four). +Drive file-write commands 0x57/0x58/0x59 hardware-verified for a single chunk only, not called by the app (writes above 16 KiB refused); 0x5A/0x5B/0x5C (move/copy/delete) not implemented. Protocol code ported from elk-herd (BSD-2, (c) mzero). Fixtures: 34 real .syx dumps. 124 commits, GPL-3.0-or-later. Not firmware modding. Windows/Linux write testing incomplete.

_Related: vendors `elk-herd` (catalogue notes: protocol code ported from elk-herd) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### digitone-syx-toolkit

Python CLI (+ Tkinter GUI) to capture, replay, diff and hex-view SysEx, and to generate Digitone II PATTERN .syx from an empty template. README (Japanese) says Digitone II only. Hardware-validated: pattern-wide mode, tracks 1-8, steps 1-128, normal trigs, pitch, velocity, length (inherit/explicit/INF), tempo/speed/total steps, import/send. Not supported: chords, track-default rewriting, condition/probability/micro timing/retrig, non-destructive editing. Length encoding per README: inherit = 0xFF, explicit INF = 0x7F, finite 0x00..0x7E. 47 commits, licence not shown.

_Sources: GitHub README, SYXGRID README_

### DNX

Browser tools (Web MIDI, Chromium only, nothing uploaded) for Digitone and Digitone II projects: Expander (each sound-locked Digitone 1 sound gets its own track on the Digitone II), Manager (move/copy/swap/clear/rename patterns across banks with undo; Insights: polymeter, PATTERN RESET cost, voice use), Library (browse/search/rename the 2,048 +Drive presets; wavetables need Digitone II with "Waverider" firmware), Backup (whole +Drive into one .dnx with a manifest; excludes global settings), Probe (read-only identification and traffic capture) and CLI commands (project, plan, convert, copy, rearrange, rename, track, rebuild, diff, sheet; dry run by default). Write safeguards: WRITE switch must be armed, copy of current contents saved first, every write read back and compared, destinations checked against a fresh listing, never writes the loaded project, never converts a DN2 preset to DN1; close Transfer and Overbridge first (shared MIDI ports). Formats: .dnprj (DN1) and .dn2prj (DN2) projects, sound banks .syx; payloads LZ4-compressed inside a ZIP; SysEx uses 8-in-7 MSB-first. Author discloses LLM use; AGPL-3.0-or-later, TypeScript, 15 stars, created 2026-09-07. Not firmware modding. Report button opens a prefilled GitHub issue. 2026-11-10 (docs/KNOWN-ISSUES): an unpaged LIST of a 256-entry table store came back cut at about 4 KB with garbage after entry 125; listings are now paged in 64s (HYPOTHESES H23). 2026-11-15 (docs/samples.md): the owner dropped the digikit runtime from DNX's builds on 2026-11-12; the sample store keeps digikit's card-store format (store v3) but the project's own firmware now writes it through a /samples route on the Data API (files in 524,288-byte parts, at most 64 MiB a file, each part read back from the card and checked by xxHash32; no read-back of a stored file, no rename or move in version 1). The id of a stored sample is the SHA-256 of the native file. 2026-11-16 (docs/samples.md): before 2026-11-16 a plan that moved a sound to a new path ran the upload first, which sent nothing, and then deleted the only copy; the old copy is now deleted just before the upload. Layout and token docs (UI only).

### Elektron Emu

Five VST3 plug-ins (Mac, Windows) that run each machine's real OS in an emulated CPU: Digitakt II, Syntakt, Analog Rytm MKII, Digitone II, Model:Cycles. Firmware not included; the user places the .syx from Elektron's site in a per-machine folder. +Drive emulated and persisted; WAV loading on DT2, Rytm and DN2. Digitone II's DSP is compiled locally on first open (needs a C compiler, else a slow interpreter that renders offline only). Caveats: Rytm analog voices/effects are a custom model that does not sound like the real machine; Syntakt analog tracks 9-12 missing; Mac builds unsigned. 2 commits, 19 stars, no licence stated. Personal project, not affiliated with Elektron (panel photos belong to Elektron).

_Sources: GitHub README, altstrument tools page_

### TERRAIN for Digitone II

Unofficial custom OS for the Digitone II that adds TERRAIN, a wave-terrain synth machine (module "terreno"), plus quality-of-life mods. Built in the browser from the user's own OS 1.12 file: a patch list copies bytes from the user's sections 3 and 7 and inserts the project's own, then checks the result's SHA-256 against the tested build and reruns Elektron's integrity checks before the download. Built with a patched digikit (40 parameters per machine, voice adapter, OS 1.12 anchors) and dnfw's container code; several mods are ported from dn2_firmware_explore. Some page glyphs were captured from the stock pages (to be replaced by calls to the firmware's own drawing). Uninstall by sending the original OS 1.12. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-14 (created that day, one commit); README read 2026-11-14. 2026-11-17: build v63e (2026-11-16) extends MOD GRAPHICS (gliding knob graphics) to the SYN pages of the stock machines by taking over the SYN page's draw method.

### RIFT (second Digitone II firmware)

A second Digitone II firmware by the dn2mk2 author, separate from that mod: no Machinedrum or Monomachine machines, starting with one engine, FASCIA (two exciters into two coupled modal bodies, TZFM, ring and frequency shift, a spectral morph, a low-pass gate). Its first commit carries the dn2mk2 infrastructure (build framework, SHARC DSL, release gate); FASCIA's model, its float32 DSP-order contract and a bit-exact SHARC program come from dn2mk2 branches. Plan (docs/rift.md): stand FASCIA alone, measure its voice count, then integrate and release. The test bench is private. Found by find_new (new repo of a catalogued author) 2026-11-13. v0.1 (2026-11-13) removes the Machinedrum and Monomachine engines from the DSP image to fit the 2 MiB upgrade buffer. The roadmap (docs/rift-roadmap.md) plans per-track insert effects, an LPG filter type, a looping function-generator envelope and a granular machine. 2026-11-15 (releases/v0.3, ROADMAP): FASCIA fits about three voices of the heaviest patches and six to eight typical ones; sample voices get DSP time first. Planned next: an ORGAN engine, SILT, per-track insert effects, a granular sampler and stereo. 2026-11-17 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.4, docs/organ.md): v0.4 ORGAN ports the pipe organ of the author's Ravel firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1 (GPL-3.0) bit-exact to a float32 reference, then to the SHARC within a stated tolerance; it runs inside FASCIA's DSP program under the same guard and costs much less than a FASCIA voice. Known issue: FASCIA with BEND up and DAMP near 0 decays unevenly and sometimes cuts a voice (keep BEND at 10 or less). Next: SILT (material synthesis), the BEND fix, the reworked FLEX, then a bead engine and a Three Sisters-style filter. 2026-11-18 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.5-v0.6, docs/organ.md, docs/silt-dsp.md): v0.5 adds two ORGAN pages that leave v0.4's organ bit for bit at 0; v0.6 adds SILT (type 20) with a DSP cost plan: per-voice DDR delay lines, a 4-voice cap with the oldest voice stolen, graceful degradation of ensemble size, cost and stress gate steps with a negative control. Known issues in v0.6: v0.5 ORGAN sounds with MIXT up change (old PHRM/VELO values read as MTUN/MCHR); FIBER plays about twice as loud as the other materials. Planned: SILT level matching, CPU guardrails for every engine, LIGATURE (a modular voice wired by the user), the reworked FLEX.

_Related: builds on `dn2mk2` (docs/rift.md: the infrastructure from dn2mk2-firmware e06993e (v0.51)) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_
